references.context: Order theory: descending chain condition (DCC) on a partially ordered collection, applied here to the poset of ideals of a commutative ring ordered by inclusion; every sequence I_1⊇I_2⊇⋯ stabilizes.
references.reason: The descending-chain condition is a reusable order-theoretic property distinct from the Artinian-ring meaning obtained by applying it to the ideal poset.
references.matching_note: Do not confuse descending-chain Artinian condition with the ascending-chain Noetherian condition, or with finiteness of the set of ideals.

references.disposition: Every chain has its own stabilization index; Artinian does not mean the ring has a finite number of ideals.

references.phrase: submodule IM generated by products I·M
references.context: Module theory over a commutative unital ring R: ideal action IM on an R-module M, the submodule of all finite sums of products i m with i∈I and m∈M; includes I^n M for ideal powers.
references.reason: IM is a reusable ideal-times-module construction required to interpret the special IM=M convention in the definition of depth.
references.matching_note: Existing candidate missing.d066de85583ac1b1a7d4 already captures this concept; alias/context review remains separate. Not the same as ideal multiplication I^n or quotient module M/IM.

references.phrase: supremum of lengths of regular sequences
references.context: Order theory: supremum of a set of nonnegative integer lengths in the extended ordered set ℕ∪{∞}, taking the least upper bound when bounded and ∞ for unbounded lengths; here lengths of M-regular sequences contained in I.
references.reason: The least-upper-bound operation on allowable sequence lengths is a reusable order-theoretic construction, while the resulting value defines depth relative to I.
references.matching_note: Compare existing generic supremum candidate missing.066b1d1b9032a2e86bdd; preserve the distinct stipulated convention depth_I(M)=∞ when IM=M.

references.disposition: This is an explicit special convention; no regular sequence maximum is sought when IM=M.

references.phrase: integral domain R and fraction field K
K-span of R-submodule M equals V
references.context: Linear algebra: K-linear span span_K(M) of a subset M of a K-vector space V, the subspace of finite K-linear combinations of members of M; the lattice condition requires span_K(M)=V.
references.reason: Spanning by K-linear combinations is a reusable vector-space construction distinct from merely being a finitely generated R-submodule or finite-dimensional K-vector space.
references.matching_note: Compare existing module-span candidate missing.beea674f8fcd201a1af5, but distinguish R-module span from extension of scalars to the fraction field K.

references.disposition: Dimension refers to Krull dimension of R, not to vector space dimension of V, which may be any finite value.
